questions.question: A line which intersects a circle in only one single point is called a:
questions.explanation: A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, known as the point of contact.

questions.question: A line which intersects a circle in two distinct points is called a:
questions.explanation: A secant line cuts through the circle, intersecting it at two distinct points.

questions.question: The radial segment drawn to the point of contact of a tangent is:
questions.explanation: Theorem 1 of Unit 10: The radius drawn to the point of contact is perpendicular to the tangent (angle = 90°).

questions.question: The number of tangents that can be drawn to a circle from a point outside it is:
questions.explanation: From any external point P, exactly two tangents (PA and PB) can be drawn to the circle.

questions.question: The lengths of two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle are:
questions.explanation: Theorem 2 of Unit 10: Two tangents drawn to a circle from an exterior point have identical lengths (PA = PB).

questions.question: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle from a point lying inside the circle?
questions.explanation: Every line through an interior point is a secant; zero tangents can be drawn.

questions.question: How many tangents can be drawn to a circle at a given point lying on the circle?
questions.explanation: At any specific point on the circumference, exactly one unique tangent line can be drawn.

questions.question: If PA and PB are two tangents from P to a circle with centre O, the quadrilateral PAOB is a/an:
questions.explanation: Since ∠PAO = ∠PBO = 90°, their sum is 180°, making opposite angles supplementary and PAOB cyclic.

questions.question: If the angle between two tangents drawn from an external point is 60°, the angle subtended by their chord of contact at the centre is:
questions.explanation: The central angle and the angle between tangents are supplementary: 180° - 60° = 120°.

questions.question: If a tangent PA of length 12 cm is drawn to a circle of radius 5 cm, the distance of P from the centre O is:
questions.explanation: Triangle OAP is right-angled at A. OP = √(OA² + PA²) = √(5² + 12²) = √(25 + 144) = √169 = 13 cm.

questions.question: Tangents drawn at the endpoints of a diameter of a circle are:
questions.explanation: Both tangents are perpendicular to the same diameter line, making them parallel to each other.

questions.question: Two circles touch each other externally. How many common tangents can be drawn to them?
questions.explanation: Two external direct common tangents plus one transverse common tangent at the point of contact = 3 common tangents.

questions.question: Two circles touch each other internally. How many common tangents can be drawn to them?
questions.explanation: There is only one common tangent passing through their single shared point of internal contact.

questions.question: Two circles intersect at two distinct points. How many common tangents can be drawn to them?
questions.explanation: Intersecting circles have exactly 2 direct common tangents.

questions.question: Two completely separate non-intersecting circles have how many common tangents?
questions.explanation: Two disjoint circles admit 2 direct and 2 transverse (internal) common tangents, totaling 4.

questions.question: The line segment joining the centres of two touching circles passes through:
questions.explanation: The centres and the point of contact are collinear.

questions.question: If two circles of radii 5 cm and 3 cm touch externally, the distance between their centres is:
questions.explanation: For externally touching circles, distance between centres d = r₁ + r₂ = 5 + 3 = 8 cm.

questions.question: If two circles of radii 7 cm and 3 cm touch internally, the distance between their centres is:
questions.explanation: For internally touching circles, distance between centres d = |r₁ - r₂| = 7 - 3 = 4 cm.

questions.question: The perpendicular to a tangent line at its point of contact passes through:
questions.explanation: The normal to a circle at any point on its circumference is the radial line, which passes through the centre.

questions.question: A circle has only one:
questions.explanation: A circle has infinitely many chords, tangents, and secants, but exactly one unique centre point.
